title: IAEA team led by Rafael Grossi departs for the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant
body:
On the morning of 29 August 2022 a team of International Atomic Energy Agency experts and inspectors led by Director General Rafael Mariano Grossi left the agency's headquarters in Vienna for Ukraine. The mission was called the IAEA Support and Assistance Mission to Zaporizhzhia, or ISAMZ. World Nuclear News reported on 30 August 2022 that the team had reached Kyiv and that its onward plans were withheld for security reasons, with the team expected to reach the plant later that week.

Russian forces had controlled the Zaporizhzhia plant since early March 2022, but Ukrainian staff continued to operate it. It was the first nuclear power plant occupied by a military force. Shelling had intensified in the preceding weeks, and both sides blamed each other. Ukraine said all safety systems remained operational and radiation levels had not risen. Units 5 and 6 were operating and the other four units were shut down.

The plant had temporarily lost its last operational external line, the 750-kilovolt Dniprovska line, which was disconnected at least twice on 25 August, disconnecting Units 5 and 6 from the grid until they were reconnected on 26 August. At the plant the team planned to assess physical damage, check main and backup safety and security systems, evaluate the conditions of control room staff and carry out urgent safeguards verification. Grossi described the situation as "highly volatile and fragile".
